claims.text: The FeNiCrCoCu coating has a single-phase FCC structure.
The FeNiCrCoCu coating has high elastic modulus and stable wear resistance at 300 K.
Dislocation slip is active at room temperature in the FCC alloy.
Deformation twinning contributes to room-temperature plasticity and stability in FeNiCrCoCu.
Strength and deformation behavior in related FCC high-entropy alloys are temperature dependent.
Deformation twinning enhances work hardening and mechanical performance.
Increasing temperature thermally reduces the stacking-fault energy of FeNiCrCoCu.
A reduction in stacking-fault energy suppresses deformation twinning.
The elevated-temperature deformation mode changes from planar slip and twinning to cross-slip and dislocation climb.
At elevated temperature, the critical stress for twinning exceeds the applied stress and twinning is suppressed.
Suppression of twinning causes a loss of work-hardening capacity.
Thermally activated dislocation climb produces rapid lattice disorder and lattice softening.
Lattice softening causes a sharp decline in yield strength and wear resistance.
There is a critical temperature at which the wear rate begins to increase exponentially.
Below the critical temperature, wear remains stable because of twin-assisted plasticity.
Above the critical temperature, dislocation climb and lattice softening dominate and cause rapid material removal.
Cu addition may alter stacking-fault energy and thermal stability relative to CrMnFeCoNi.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that thermal energy overcomes the critical resolved shear stress for twinning, whereas the mechanism states that the critical twinning stress exceeds the applied stress as temperature rises. These imply opposite effects on whether twinning should activate.

The initial-state and baseline fields describe room-temperature twinning only as potential, while the mechanism treats an active slip–twinning balance as the established source of room-temperature stability.
